newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, Dec up on firm cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, Dec up on firm cash.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures settled mixed, with December live cattle supported by firm cash cattle prices, CME floor traders said.
Cash cattle at southern Plains feedyards sold steady at $71.00 per cwt, and midday wholesale beef quotes were higher, according to USDA data.

Tight supplies of fed cattle continued to bolster cash markets and nearby futures contracts, sources said. Wednesday's USDA-estimated slaughter at 126,000 head was at the low end of analysts' estimates and well below last year's rate of 135,000, head.
Late weakness in the market was linked to both speculative profit taking on long positions and commercial selling, pit sources said.
Many traders said fed cattle trade was virtually finished for the week.
R.B. & H. Financial Services was a noted seller, R.J O'Brien & Assoc. was a late seller and Refco was on both sides of the market, pit sources said.
Some floor traders said the market is beginning to feel a little toppy, and some that believe the market is poised for a seasonal slide were late sellers, they said.
Strong resistance was seen at 66.85 cents a lb, which was Wednesday's 40-day moving average and the settlement price for December live cattle, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures were underpinned by early gains in live cattle as well as a small jump in the CME feeder cattle index.
The CME index for Monday climbed $0.09 to $62.06 per cwt.

December live cattle closed up 0.175 at 66.850 cents per lb, and other contracts were down 0.100 to down 0.070 cent. November feeder cattle settled up 0.075 at 62.275 cents, with other contracts down 0.050 to up 0.070 cent.
